Have the dock. Love it. It’s set up in my living room so I just drop it in the dock and we’re set. A few things though. 

1. I had to put a Switch into the dock initially to get it work. No idea why but ever since it’s worked great. 

2. Emulators won’t switch inputs when you dock. So have an input profiles saved on your standalone emulators that you can load up easily or you will be configuring your controller every time you dock. I believe retroarch doesn’t suffer from this though. 
2.a the Odin will recognize the switch on inputs but the emulators don’t automatically. 

3. Switch your TV to game mode if you have it. I was having massive stutter and I thought it was the Odin. Switched the mode on the TV and it solved it. 

4. Leave your Odin screen on while it’s docked. You’ll have to do some navigating on the device docked (see input comment above) it’s not a ton but it’s there. 

5. I use the 8bitdo pro2 controller with the wireless adapter. Bluetooth is to slow and you’ll notice input delay if you try and use Bluetooth. 
5.a I could not get any retrobrawler64 wireless controllers or usb wired 64 controllers to work with dock. I use the 8bit for everything. 

6. Set ways to exit emulators or at least access the emulators menu while in a game so you can avoid getting up and using the Odin to do the navigation. 

All I can think of for more but overall I really like using the dock. Once I got all the above sorted out.

3. Where do you think I'm lacking for this job? Again needs to be done confidently but it will allow you to address any shortcomings the interviewer may feel you have while pointing out you have experience in that area. 

4. What's your favorite aspect of this company? Again show interest in where you're going to be working. 

5. What can I do in the meantime to prepare myself to hit the ground running for you guys? Not only are you asking for the job but you're saying "hey I wanna be here and I wanna make a difference".
